content: The World Rapid Chess Championship was held in 2017, and the current world rapid champion is Indian grandmaster Vishwanathan Anand, who won the title on December 28, 2017 [5]. There is no information provided in the documents regarding who specifically won the rapid chess championship in Riyadh in 2017.

The United States left the gold standard in March and April 1933 [3][5]. In a series of laws and executive orders, the government suspended the gold standard for United States currency [5]. After this, the US would no longer pay gold on demand for the dollar, and gold would no longer be considered valid legal tender for debts in private and public contracts [5].

The Svalbard Global Seed Vault was officially opened on February 26, 2008 [2]. Before the vault's construction, the Nordic Gene Bank had been storing backup Nordic plant germplasm via frozen seeds in an abandoned coal mine at Svalbard since 1984 [4]. The vault is located on the Norwegian island of Spitsbergen near Longyearbyen [5].

Patrick S. Castagne [1][2] composed the national anthem of Trinidad and Tobago, titled "Forged from the Love of Liberty," in 1962 [1]. The anthem was originally composed as the national anthem for the short-lived West Indies Federation (1958–1962) [1]. Castagne, a renowned West Indian songwriter, was employed at the Trinidad and Tobago Commission in London when he composed the anthem [1]. The anthem was adopted by Trinidad and Tobago after the country gained independence on August 31, 1962 [2].

The famous street in New Orleans is Bourbon Street, a historic street in the French Quarter, known for its numerous bars and strip clubs [1]. St. Charles Avenue is another prominent thoroughfare, famous for the mansions that line its tree-lined boulevard [2]. Royal Street, located in the French Quarter, is known for its antique shops, art galleries, and hotels [3][5]. Frenchmen Street in the Faubourg Marigny neighborhood is known for its live-music venues and other businesses [4].

The song "Do You Want to Know a Secret?" was sung by George Harrison of the Beatles [1]. It was primarily composed by John Lennon but credited to Lennon–McCartney [1]. The United States top ten song version was released by Vee-Jay [1]. Harrison also sang another song on the Beatles' "Please Please Me" album, "Chains" [3]. The song was originally written by Lennon–McCartney [1].

The Thirteenth Amendment to the United States Constitution, which abolished slavery, was ratified by the required number of states on December 6, 1865 [2]. The amendment was later proclaimed adopted by Secretary of State William H. Seward on December 18, 1865 [2]. It was passed by the Senate on April 8, 1864, and by the House on January 31, 1865 [2]. The Thirteenth Amendment became part of the Constitution on December 6, 1865, based on the ratifications from 27 of the 36 states, including those that had been "in rebellion" [1].

The song "Don't Matter to Me" by Drake featuring posthumous vocals from Michael Jackson was released on Drake's fifth studio album "Scorpion" in 2018 [1][2]. It was sent to British contemporary hit radio on July 6, 2018 as the album's fourth single [1][2].

The 1966 FIFA World Cup, held in England from 11 to 30 July 1966, saw England win the tournament with a 4–2 victory over West Germany [1]. It is England's only FIFA World Cup title [1]. The game was played on home soil [1]. England won the Jules Rimet Trophy in this tournament [1].

Booker T. Washington was addressing an audience at the Atlanta Exposition in his speech given on September 18, 1895 [3]. The speech was aimed at both African-Americans and whites, as he called on African-Americans to join the workforce and encouraged whites to invest in the South's industrials rather than relying on immigrants [2]. The speech laid the foundation for the Atlanta compromise, an agreement between African-American leaders and Southern white leaders [3].

Alabama became a right-to-work state in the 1976 legislative session [2]. Edward J. Steimel, the founding executive director of the Louisiana Association of Business and Industry, pushed for the passage of the legislation [3]. Louisiana was the last traditional southern state to adopt such legislation [2]. The fight over the legislation culminated in its 1976 passage [3].

The first North American Indigenous Games were held in Edmonton, Alberta, Canada in 1990 [1]. The event was governed by the North American Indigenous Games Council, a 26-member council of representatives from various provinces and territories in Canada and the United States [2]. The dream to hold such a Games for Indigenous peoples of North America began in the 1970s [2]. The 2017 North American Indigenous Games were held in Toronto, Ontario, Canada [3]. The Games featured 5000 athletes aged 13 to 19 in 14 sports [3].

The Dark Tower series by Stephen King consists of eight books, incorporating themes from multiple genres such as dark fantasy, science fantasy, horror, and Western [1][2]. In addition to the eight novels in the series proper, many of King's other books also relate to the story [1]. King has also confirmed that the idea for a new Dark Tower novel exists and this novel is scheduled to be written in about eight months, with a tentative title being "The Wind Through the Keyhole" [3]. The final book in the series, The Dark Tower VII: The Dark Tower, was published on King's birthday, September 21, 2004, and has four subtitles [5].

The Ferris wheel, known as the Myrtle Beach SkyWheel, is located in Myrtle Beach, South Carolina [1][4]. It opened on May 20th, 2011 and at the time of its construction, it was the tallest Ferris wheel in the United States east of the Mississippi River [1]. The wheel was designed by Ronald Bussink Professional Rides and manufactured by Chance Morgan [1]. The Myrtle Beach SkyWheel is similar in design to the Niagara SkyWheel and the Seattle Great Wheel [1].
The third season of Rick and Morty aired on Cartoon Network's adult-oriented late night programming block, Adult Swim [1][2]. The episodes originally aired on Sundays at 11:30 p.m EST [2].

The term that refers to linking a currency value to the value of gold is known as the gold standard [1][2]. Under this system, a country's government declares that it will exchange its currency for a certain weight in gold [2]. In a pure gold standard, anyone can enter the central bank and exchange coins or currency for pure gold or vice versa [2]. The gold standard works under the assumption that there are no restrictions on capital movements or export of gold by private citizens across countries [2].

The first Olympic football (soccer) competition was held in 1900 [5]. The 1900 tournament was followed by competitions in the 1904 Summer Olympics and the 1906 Intercalated Games [5]. However, the Olympic football tournament was only officially recognized as a FIFA-supervised event starting in the 1908 Summer Olympics [5].

The Cleveland Browns returned to the NFL in 1999 after a three-year period of deactivation [1]. The Browns were reactivated with Lerner, a friend of Art Modell and a minority owner of Modell's original franchise, assuming ownership [2]. The 1999 Cleveland Browns season marked the return of professional football to Cleveland [3]. The Browns are considered a continuation of the previous franchise, as the history and colors of the team remained in Cleveland [3].

St. Petersburg is a city in Pinellas County, Florida, United States [1][2]. It is the fifth-most populous city in Florida and the largest in the state that is not a county seat [1][2]. St. Petersburg is located on the Pinellas peninsula between Tampa [1]. Pinellas County is part of the Tampa–St. Petersburg–Clearwater, Florida Metropolitan Statistical Area [3].

In 1888, George Eastman introduced the first handheld amateur camera, the Kodak camera [3]. It was marketed with the slogan "You press the button, we do the rest" [3]. A hand-held Lumière camera was used to film Wilbur Wright flying his aircraft in Paris in 1908 [1]. Thomas Edison developed a portable film camera in 1896 [1]. The compact hand-cranked Parvo camera was first made in Paris [4]. The camera obscura, an early device that projected images, had been in existence since at least the 16th century [5].

Anne Hathaway plays the White Queen, named Mirana of Marmoreal, in Tim Burton's 2010 adaptation of "Alice Through the Looking Glass" [1]. Hathaway described her interpretation of the White Queen as a punk-rock vegan pacifist [2]. The White Queen's soldiers appear in white armor inspired by chess pieces [1]. The White Queen's delicate exterior is reinforced by her habit of holding her hands gracefully in almost every scene [1]. In the film, Alice initially thinks she is having a recurring dream, but accepts her destiny and slays the Jabberwocky, restoring the White Queen's rulership of Wonderland [3].

The South Carolina Ordinance of Secession was written by a group of delegates from the state [1][4]. Christopher Memminger was asked to write the "Declaration of the Immediate Causes Which Induce and Justify the Secession of South Carolina from the Federal Union", which outlined the reasons for secession [1]. William Henry Gist called for a secession convention to be held in Columbia on December 17, 1860, and was one of the signers of the Ordinance of Secession on December 20, 1860 [2].

The cost to host the 2016 Summer Olympics in Rio was USD 4.6 billion [1][4]. This figure includes direct capital costs, such as competition venues, the Olympic village, international broadcast center, and media and press center [1]. Indirect capital costs, such as for road, rail, or airport infrastructure, were not included [1]. The Rio Olympics' cost compares with costs of USD 40–44 billion for Beijing 2008 and USD 51 billion for Sochi 2014 [1].

The festival of Holi marks the end of winter and the beginning of spring [1][2]. It is celebrated to celebrate the arrival of spring and the good harvest [1][2]. In some literature, Holi wasIdentified as a festival that celebrated agriculture [2]. It is also a time to enjoy spring's abundant colors and say farewell to winter [3]. The festival has traditionally been observed by non-Hindus, such as Jains and Newar Buddhists [5]. Sikhs have also traditionally celebrated Holi, at least through the 19th century [5]. Guru Gobind Singh – the last human guru of the Sikhs – modified Holi with a three-day Hola Mohalla extension festival of martial arts [5].

The song "Brown Eyes" is from Fleetwood Mac's 1979 double LP "Tusk" [4]. It was one of six songs composed and sung by Christine McVie [4]. In the song "Pretty Brown Eyes," Australian-born United States-resident, pop singer, Cody Simpson co-wrote the song with songwriting duo Timothy and Theron Thomas, and Vasquez Castillo [2][3]. La Toya Jackson wrote "Brown Eyes" for Jimmy Cliff's album [5].

The winner of Big Brother 11 was Jordan [2]. In Big Brother 14, Frank was the winner of the $25,000 America's Favorite HouseGuest prize [1]. In Big Brother 19, Josh Martinez won the game in a 5–4 vote against Paul Abrahamian [3]. In Big Brother 13, Rachel won the final Head of Household (HOH) competition and was crowned the winner by a jury vote of 4–3 [4]. In Big Brother 10, Dan was crowned the winner with a Jury vote of seven to zero [5].

The Gadsden Purchase is a region of present-day southern Arizona and southwestern New Mexico that the United States purchased via a treaty signed on December 30, 1853, by James Gadsden, U.S. ambassador to Mexico, and by Antonio López de Santa Anna, president of Mexico [1]. The U.S. Senate approved the purchase on April 25, 1854 [1]. The price for the purchase was $10 million [4]. The transaction took effect on June 8, 1854 [1].

The Royal Flying Doctor Service (RFDS) was established by Reverend John Flynn on May 15, 1928, in Cloncurry, Queensland [1]. This date marks the official start of the RFDS, which was a one-year experiment based in Cloncurry, Queensland, launched by Flynn's Australian Inland Mission Aerial Medical Service [1][2].

The song "Genie in a Bottle" was released on June 22, 1999, by RCA Records [1]. It was the lead single from Christina Aguilera's self-titled debut album [1]. The single reached number one on the "Billboard" Hot 100 and stayed there for five consecutive weeks [2]. Overall, it was one of the biggest hits of the summer of 1999 [2].

The second season of "Jessica Jones" was released on March 8, 2018, on Netflix worldwide in Ultra HD 4K and high dynamic range [1]. The teaser trailer for the season was released in December 2017, along with announcing the season release date [1]. The season premiered in November 2015, with episodes receiving critical acclaim [3]. The third season is scheduled to be released in 2019 [3]. The season is set in the Marvel Cinematic Universe [4].

The end of Roman rule in Britain was marked by a series of events that took place in different parts of Britain at different times [1]. In 383, the usurper Magnus Maximus withdrew troops from northern and western Britain, possibly leaving local warlords in charge [1]. Around 410, the Romano-Britons expelled the magistrates of the usurper Constantine III in response to his failures to protect the island [1][2]. The Roman Emperor Honorius replied to a request for assistance with the "Rescript" [1].

During the 2012 Summer Olympics opening ceremony, the torch was carried into the Olympic Stadium by Steve Redgrave [2]. Redgrave then passed the torch to a team of six young athletes and one young volunteer, each nominated by a famous British Olympian [1]. These seven young athletes then applied their torch to one of the 204 petals of the Olympic cauldron [2].

The Latin word "camera obscura" (plural "camera obscura" or "camera obscuras"; from Latin, meaning "dark room": "camera" "(vaulted) chamber or room," and "obscura" "dark") describes a natural optical phenomenon that occurs when an image of a scene at the other side of a screen is projected through a small hole in that screen as a reversed and inverted image on a surface opposite to the opening [1][2][3]. The surroundings of the projected image have to be relatively dark for the image to be clear [1]. Camera obscura devices have been used since the second half of the 16th century as an aid for drawing and painting [4].

The 1912 Boston Red Sox season holds the record for the most games won in a season by the team with 105 wins and 47 losses [3]. The team also set a franchise record for highest winning percentage in a season at .691 [3]. The 2018 Boston Red Sox surpassed the prior mark of 105 wins that had been set in 1912, and also won the most games by any MLB team since the 2001 Seattle Mariners won 116 [2].

The ninth series of Britain's Got Talent, aired between April 11 to May 31, 2015, was won by dog tricks duo Jules O'Dwyer & Matisse [1]. This series saw the "Wildcard" feature updated, allowing both the judges and the public to vote for eliminated acts to proceed to the final [3]. However, viewers complained about being misled by winner O'Dwyer's performance, as her act involved a second dog that was not disclosed [1].

Cricket was introduced to India by the East India Company [1]. The earliest reference to cricket being played in the Indian sub-continent is dated April 1721, when British sailors of the East India Company were reported to be playing cricket at Cambay, near Baroda [3]. The Oriental Cricket Club, a cricket club established by the Parsi community in Mumbai in 1848, is considered the origin of Indian cricket [4].
Matt Brody was played by an actor in the original "Baywatch" television series [1]. In the 2017 film adaptation of the show, the character of Matt Brody is played by Cop Garner Ellerbee [2].

The Black Stallion is the title character from author Walter Farley's book series about an Arab stallion and its young owner, Alec Ramsay [2]. In the books, the Black Stallion is referred to as the Black or Shêtân [2]. According to a different source, the Black Stallion in the 1979 film is a wild Arabian stallion [3]. The Phantom Stallion, a different character, is described as being half Quarter Horse and Half Mustang [1]. The Phantom Stallion was originally solid black and named Blackie [1].

The most plentiful type of rock in Earth's crust is igneous rock, making up approximately 64.7% of the Earth's crust by volume [1]. Of these, about 66% are basalts and gabbros, 16% are granite, and 17% granodiorites and diorites [1]. The oceanic crust is composed of dense (mafic) iron magnesium silicate igneous rocks, like basalt [2].

Elvin Bishop wrote and performed "Fooled Around and Fell in Love" [1][2]. However, Bishop did not sing lead vocals on the track; he invited vocalist Mickey Thomas, a background singer in his band at the time, to sing it [1]. The song was released as a single in 1976 and peaked at #3 on the "Billboard" Hot 100 singles chart [1].

The song "As Time Goes By" was written by Herman Hupfeld in 1931 [1][3]. It gained fame in 1942 when it was sung by the character Sam (Dooley Wilson) in the movie "Casablanca" [1][3]. The song has since become a representative song of Warner Bros. and was featured in various films and television shows [1][3].

A systolic blood pressure value is the pressure measurement in the arteries that occurs near the end of the cardiac cycle, when the ventricles are contracting [1]. This value is achieved through various methods, such as using a sphygmomanometer to listen for the sound of blood flow within the arteries [4], and understanding the pressure varies with each heartbeat [1]. A healthy, resting adult human's systolic blood pressure might, for example, be 120 mmHg [1][5].

The singer Marion Raven, whose surname means "raven," married professional snowboarder Andreas Wiig in 2013, but they later divorced in 2015 [1]. It is not clear who the character Raven in the show That's So Raven is married to, as there is no information about her personal life provided in the documents searched.
"There Will Be Blood" is a 2007 American drama film directed by Paul Thomas Anderson [2]. The film takes place during Southern California's oil boom of the late 19th and early 20th centuries [2].

In the first-ever Monday Night Football game, which was telecast in 1970 [1][5], the Cleveland Browns defeated the New York Jets with a score of 31-21 [1]. This game marked the debut of Monday Night Football on ABC [5].

The New England Patriots have won three Super Bowl championships in four years [1][4]. Specifically, they won in 2001, 2003, and 2004 [1]. However, they did not win the Super Bowl in a row [2]. The last team that won two Super Bowls in a row was the Seattle Seahawks, who defeated the Panthers in 2014, but ultimately lost to the Patriots in Super Bowl XLIX the following year [2]. The Patriots' chance of winning three consecutive Super Bowl championships ended in 2006, when they lost to the Broncos in the playoffs [3].

In networking, NAT stands for Network Address Translation [1][2][3]. It is a method of remapping one IP address space into another by modifying network address information in the IP header of packets while they are in transit across a traffic routing device [1][2]. This technique is used to conserve global address space in the face of IPv4 address exhaustion and allows one Internet-routable IP address of a NAT gateway to be used for an entire private network [1]. The term "NAT" has become virtually synonymous with IP masquerading [3].

The third How to Train Your Dragon movie is scheduled for release on February 22, 2019 [2]. The release date was initially set for 2016, but had several delays [4]. The film's title was changed to How to Train Your Dragon: The Hidden World in April 2018 [2].

"I'm Not Gonna Miss You" is a song recorded by American country music artist Glen Campbell and The Wrecking Crew [1][2]. Co-written by Campbell and producer Julian Raymond, the song was released on September 30, 2014 for the soundtrack to the documentary "Glen Campbell: I'll Be Me" [1]. The song was nominated for Best Original Song at the 87th Academy Awards [1][2].
In the 2000 live-action film "How the Grinch Stole Christmas!", Cindy Lou Who is played by actress Taylor Momsen [1].

The rib eye steak comes from the rib section of a beef animal, specifically from ribs six through twelve [1][3]. More specifically, the rib eye steak is mostly composed of the longissimus dorsi muscle but also contains the complexus and spinalis muscles [1]. The original rib eye steak was the center portion of the rib steak without the bone [2]. In Australia and New Zealand, the ribeye is served with the bone in and is called "ribeye"; when the bone is removed, it is called "Scotch fillet" [3].

The Lion King debuted on Broadway at the New Amsterdam Theater on October 15, 1997 [1][2] with previews, and had its official opening on November 13, 1997 [1]. The show is still running after more than 8,500 performances [1].

The Golden State Warriors are an American professional basketball team based in Oakland, California [1][2]. Founded in 1946 in Philadelphia, the Warriors relocated to the San Francisco Bay Area in 1962 and changed its geographic moniker to Golden State in 1971 [1]. They play their home games at the Oracle Arena [1]. The team'sclusive home court was established in Oakland in 1971 [3].

The music for How to Train Your Dragon was composed by John Powell [1][3][4]. The soundtrack was released by Varèse Sarabande on March 23, 2010 [1]. The score was well received by film score critics [4]. Jónsi wrote and performed the song "Sticks & Stones" for the film [4].

The first man-made object to enter space was a German V-2 rocket, on a flight in October 1942 [2]. The rocket changed direction perfectly during this launch and landed 193 km away [2]. The first liquid-fueled rocket to take flight was launched by Robert Goddard on March 16, 1926, in Auburn, Massachusetts [4]. The rocket reached an altitude of 41 feet and traveled 184 feet in 2.5 seconds [4].

Hungry Jack's, a franchise of Burger King Corporation, operates or sub-licenses 390 stores in Australia [1][4]. The company is owned and operated by Competitive Foods Australia, a privately held company owned by Jack Cowin [1]. Hungry Jack's is the second largest franchisee of Burger King in the world [4]. The company is responsible for licensing new operators, opening its own stores, and performing standards oversight for franchised locations in Australia [4].

The song "You Know Better Than I" is performed by Joseph, as portrayed by David Campbell, in the 2000 direct-to-video film "Joseph: King of Dreams" [2][3]. The song is performed when Joseph is at his lowest point, and he decides to trust fully in God and acknowledge that God has an ultimate plan [2]. The song conveys the message that persevering through difficult times can yield great rewards [2].

The song "If I Were a Boy" was originally written by BC Jean and Toby Gad [1][5]. Jean initially recorded the ballad herself, but her record company rejected it [1][5]. Beyoncé later recorded her own version of the song and it became a popular single from Beyoncé's third studio album, "I Am... Sasha Fierce" [1].

"10 Things I Hate About You" is a 1999 American teen romantic comedy-drama film set in a high school in the Seattle metropolitan area [1]. Many scenes were filmed at Stadium High School in Tacoma [1][4]. The film was released on March 31, 1999 [1].

In association football, substitutions are generally made during a stoppage in play with the permission of the referee [3]. The outgoing player must leave the field before the incoming player can enter [3]. Most competitions limit each team to a maximum of three substitutions [1]. In contrast, the United States national beach soccer team can make as many substitutions as they want during play, with each substitution taking place while the play is still going on [2]. In some sports, such as ice hockey and basketball, substitutions are permitted during play without a stoppage [4]. In baseball and association football (soccer), substitutions are only permitted during stoppages of play, and a player who has been substituted cannot re-enter the game [4].

The highest natural point in Texas is Guadalupe Peak, which has an elevation of above sea level [1]. It is located in Guadalupe Mountains National Park and is part of the Guadalupe Mountains range in southeastern New Mexico and West Texas [1]. The Franklin Mountains State Park in El Paso, Texas, also has a significant elevation, with the highest peak within the park being North Franklin Mountain at 7,192 feet [2].

The book An Essay on the Principle of Population was first published anonymously in 1798, with the author later identified as Thomas Robert Malthus [1]. The book, which predicted a grim future due to population growth doubling every 25 years [1], was written by Malthus [1]. The author of the essay was identified as Rev. T.R. Malthus, A.M., F.R.S. [3].
Bruce Springsteen performed at the Super Bowl XLIII halftime show [1][3]. This performance took place in 2009 [1]. Springsteen had previously turned down invitations to play at the Super Bowl [1].

Season 1 of Sherlock consists of three 90-minute episodes [1]. These episodes were initially planned to air in 2010 [1]. The original pilot episode was not aired but was included on the DVD of the first series [1].
The movie Summer of '42 was filmed on Nantucket Island, off the coast of Cape Cod [2]. Some scenes were also filmed in Greenwood, MS and other local communities [1].

The region now known as Mumbai was called "Bombaim" by the Portuguese [1][3][4]. This name possibly originated as the Galician-Portuguese phrase "bom baim", meaning "good little bay" [4]. In 1516, Portuguese explorer Duarte Barbosa used the name "Tana-Maiambu", with "Maiambu" referring to "Mumbadevi" [4].

In the TV series Still Game, Winston moves to an exterior set in Glasgow North Media Park, Maryhill, between series three and four [1]. In a different context, Winston Place, a cricketer who played Tests in 1948, was born in Rawtenstall [2].

The ratio of the wave height to its wave length is called the significant wave height (SWH or "H") [1][2][3]. It is defined as the mean wave height (trough to crest) of the highest third of the waves [1][3]. Nowadays, it is commonly defined as four times the standard deviation of the surface elevation [1]. The symbol "H" is used for this latter definition [1].
The Knicks won their last NBA championship in 1973 [1]. They reclaimed the title in a 4-1 series against the Los Angeles Lakers [1]. Their next NBA Finals appearance was in 1994 [1].

Disneyland Paris comprises two theme parks [2]. The original theme park of the complex is Disneyland Park, which opened with the resort on 12 April 1992 [3]. A second theme park, Walt Disney Studios Park, opened in 2002 [3].

During the 1890s, ragtime music began to become popular in the United States [1][2]. Originating from jigs and march music played by African American bands, ragtime is a synthesis of African syncopation and European classical music, particularly the marches made popular by John Philip Sousa [3]. Although initially denounced as degenerate by conservatives and classically trained establishments [1], ragtime gained widespread popularity and became mainstream [1][2]. It was popularized by Tin Pan Alley in the late 19th century [1].

The men's single figure skating competition of the 2018 Winter Olympics was held on 16 and 17 February 2018 at the Gangneung Ice Arena in Gangneung, South Korea [1]. With his victory at the 2018 Winter Olympics, Yuzuru Hanyu became the first male figure skater to win two consecutive gold medals [1]. The short program was held on 16 February and the free skating was held on 17 February [1].

The Ukrainian Army unveiled its new uniforms on 24 August 2016 [1]. The new uniforms in the Ukrainian Army are modeled on British military styles [1]. The new uniforms were unveiled on Independence Day of Ukraine [1]. The Army Combat Uniform patterned in Operational Camouflage Pattern (OCP) first became available to U.S. Army soldiers on 1 July 2015 [2]. The United States Air Force personnel will begin transition from their current uniforms to OCP uniforms beginning 1 October 2018 [2]. The new version of 'Army Greens' based on uniforms worn during World War II will become the standard garrison service uniform for the United States Army as of 11 November 2018 [5].

The Philadelphia Phillies won the World Series in 1980, in game 6 on October 21, after defeating the Kansas City Royals [1]. They had finished the regular season with a record of 91 wins and 71 losses, winning the National League East title by just one game over the Montreal Expos [1]. The team went on to defeat the Houston Astros in the NLCS to gain their first NL title since 1950 [1].

Jessica Bowman played the role of Colleen Cooper on Dr. Quinn, Medicine Woman [1][2][3][5]. Erika Flores played the first Colleen Cooper in the TV series, but left the role in 1995, in the middle of the third season [2]. Jessica Bowman took over the role in season three, episode 15 [5].
The process of creating a complementary RNA strand from DNA in cells is called transcription [1]. The enzyme responsible for this process is DNA-directed RNA polymerase [2][3].

The third season of RuPaul's Drag Race All Stars premiered on January 25, 2018 [1][2][3]. The season featured ten contestants,including Aja, BenDeLaCreme, Chi Chi DeVayne, Kennedy Davenport, Milk, Morgan McMichaels, Shangela, Thorgy Thor, Trixie Mattel, and season one winner BeBe Zahara Benet [1].

Piper Chapman is a fictional character in the Netflix series "Orange Is the New Black" [2][3]. She is played by Taylor Schilling [2][3][4]. The series is based on the non-fiction book "" by Piper Kerman, who is also the author of the memoir [1][2].

The first commercial cellular phone service began operation in the United States in 1983 [2]. The first commercially available cellular phone small enough to be easily carried was the Motorola DynaTAC, which was produced by a team led by Martin Cooper, a former general manager for the systems division at Motorola [3]. The first call made from this phone was placed on April 3, 1973, by Martin Cooper to Dr. Joel S. Engel of Bell Labs [4]. The Motorola DynaTAC 8000x was released in the USA a decade later in 1983 [5].

In the film The Sound of Music, the family von Trapp escapes by car to the Swiss border, where they continue on foot across the frontier into Switzerland to safety and freedom [1]. The final scene of the film shows the family hiking on the Obersalzberg near Berchtesgaden in Germany [2]. In reality, the family simply walked to the local train station and boarded a train to Italy [4].

In the first series of Broadchurch, the murderer was revealed to be Joe Miller, the husband of DS Ellie Miller [2]. The reveal was seen by 8.8 million viewers at the start of the final episode, with a peak of 9.3 million viewers [3]. The series averaged 7.1 million live viewers during its run in the UK, with 9.2 million viewers overall after accounting for time-delayed viewing [3].

The character of the mayor in the 2016 Ghostbusters film is played by an unnamed character, as the actor is not specifically mentioned in the provided search result [1]. The document does, however, mention Mayor Bradley and his secretary Jennifer Lynch, who are involved in the story's plot [1].

The song "Wall to Wall" was recorded by American singer Chris Brown for his second studio album "Exclusive" (2007) [1][2]. It was produced by Sean Garrett and Walter Scott [1]. The song failed to attain chart success in the United States, peaking at number 79 on the "Billboard" Hot 100 [1]. However, it peaked at number 21 on the Australian Singles Chart [2] and spent ten weeks on the chart [2]. In Switzerland, the song spent only four weeks on the singles chart, peaking at number 87 in its last week [2]. The music video for "Wall to Wall" was inspired by Michael Jackson's "Thriller" and the 1998 film "Blade" [3]. The remix of the song features American rapper Jadakiss [3].

In addition, a song with a similar title, "Talkin' to the Wall", was originally recorded by country singer Warner MacPherson in 1966 [4]. It was covered by American country music artist Lynn Anderson in 1974 [4]. "Talkin' to the Wall" peaked at number 3 on the Country Singles chart [4]. It also reached number 1 on the "Billboard" Hot Country Singles chart [4].
Argentina has won the FIFA World Cup twice, in 1978 and 1986 [1][4]. Argentina was also a runner-up in 1930, 1990, and 2014 [1].

Mat Hoffman landed the first successful 900 on a skateboard at a competition in Canada in 1989, as recorded in film [1]. Tony Hawk subsequently landed "The 900" at the 1999 X-Games after ten failed attempts [2].

The longest and most expensive criminal trial in the history of the United States legal system was the McMartin preschool trial, which lasted seven years and cost $15 million [1]. The trial for Giacomo "Jackie" DiNorscio, a member of the Philadelphia and later the Lucchese crime families, was also famously known for being the longest federal trial in history, lasting 21 months [3]. The trial for Industrial Bio-Test Laboratories was also one of the longest criminal trials in US history [4]. A traffic circle is a type of intersection that directs both turning and through traffic onto a one-way circular roadway, typically built for traffic calming or aesthetics [1][2]. It differs from a roundabout in that entering traffic at a traffic circle might be controlled by stop signs, traffic signals, or not be formally controlled [1][2]. In contrast, a roundabout gives priority to traffic already on the junction [3]. Roundabouts are designed to reduce the likelihood and severity of collisions by reducing traffic speeds and minimizing T-bone and head-on collisions [3]. Traffic circles may operate at higher speeds and give priority to entering traffic [5]. Some older traffic circles allow entry at higher speeds without deflection, or require a stop and a 90-degree turn to enter [5].

The Second Epistle to the Thessalonians is a book from the New Testament [1]. It is traditionally attributed to Paul the Apostle [1]. However, modern biblical scholarship is divided on whether Paul was the author or not [1]. Some scholars question its authenticity based on what they observe [1]. Murphy-O'Connor asserts that the arguments against the authenticity of 2 Thessalonians are "drastically weakened" when the text of an interpolated letter is removed and the two letters are compared [2]. Those who believe Paul was the author of 2 Thessalonians also note that the traditional ascription of the letter to Paul is preferable [2]. Additionally, some argue that Colossians, 2 Thessalonians, 1 Timothy, 2 Timothy, and Titus may have been written by Paul's followers after his death, or by members of the Pauline school a generation after his death [3].The consensus in modern New Testament scholarship is on a core group of authentic Pauline epistles: Romans, 1 and 2 Corinthians, Galatians, Philippians, 1 Thessalonians, and Philemon [5]. Several additional letters bearing Paul's name are disputed among scholars [5].

The Pax Romana refers to a long period of relative peace and stability experienced by the Roman Empire between the accession of Caesar Augustus, founder of the Roman principate, and the death of Marcus Aurelius, last of the "good emperors" [3]. This period, also called the Pax Augusta, lasted approximately 206 years (27 BC to AD 180) [3]. The Roman Empire achieved its greatest territorial extent and its population reached a maximum of up to 70 million during this time [3].

The name Pax Romana has also been associated with an international lay Catholic movement [1][2]. This organization, formed in 1921, was created by student leaders from 23 countries in response to the aftermath of World War I [4]. The motto of Pax Romana is ""Pax Christi in regno Christi"" (Latin), which translates to "peace of Christ in the kingdom of Christ" [4]. Pax Romana has a special consultative status with ECOSOC (Economic, Social and Cultural Council) of the United Nations and is a recognized private organization before the Canon Law of the Catholic Church [5].

Tornadoes are more common in the United States than any other country, with more than 1,200 tornadoes occurring annually [1]. Most tornadoes in the United States occur east of the Rocky Mountains, with the Great Plains, the Midwest, the Mississippi Valley, and the southern United States being particularly vulnerable [1]. Tornadoes have been recorded in every U.S state, including Alaska and Hawaii [2]. The states with the most tornadoes per unit area are Florida and Oklahoma [3][4]. Texas has the highest number of tornadoes overall [4]. Tornadoes in the Pacific Northwest are usually weak, with strong tornadoes such as the one that occurred in Washington in 2018 being extremely rare [5].
